question: Should verified publisher-feed following, its `publisher` CLI, and durable shared-state schema be accepted as a generic OpenClaw core capability, or should the workflow move behind a ClawHub/owner plugin boundary?
rationale: This is a new persistent public workflow with a remote trust boundary; code review cannot safely choose its permanent product and ownership boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Confirm a generic core capability
options.body: Keep the core workflow only with an explicit generic contract, reconciled DSSE foundation, and real producer-to-consumer proof.

options.title: Move owner-specific behavior out of core
options.body: Keep only any demonstrated generic extension seam in core and ship the ClawHub publisher workflow through its owner plugin or package.

options.title: Pause the stack
options.body: Defer the feature until the hosted-feed RFC and producer implementation settle the supported publisher contract.

recommendation.title: Confirm a generic core capability
recommendation.body: Keep the core workflow only with an explicit generic contract, reconciled DSSE foundation, and real producer-to-consumer proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the available feature-origin contact for the stacked implementation and can supply the requested architecture context and proof.
